A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GS/GAS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GS/GAS generation results on six datasets, method ablations, and appendix experiments on transfer, training efficiency, and inference costs.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original component ablations, diversity measurements, low-NFE experiments, and learned-timestep analyses.

M1.justification: The GS parameterization, theoretical coefficient corrections, learned and decoupled timesteps, and distillation-plus-relativistic-GAN objective remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Additional explanations and experimental ablation variants do not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10, FFHQ, AFHQv2, LSUN-Bedroom, ImageNet, and MS-COCO for the same generation tasks, including retained cross-dataset transfer experiments. New sampling budgets and diversity measurements extend evaluation within this coverage.

E2.justification: The main baseline roster is retained. v2 adds CD to a direct CIFAR10 FID/coverage comparison in Table 9, beyond its appearance in v1's efficiency comparison, and adds S4S LMS alongside LMS+PC in the controlled FFHQ comparison in Table 10.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation protocols with precision, recall, density, and coverage measurements; 50,000 generated versus 50,000 teacher images on ImageNet; and coverage evaluation using 10,000 generated images against CIFAR10's test set. It also adds NFE=1–2 evaluations and controlled initialization/training comparisons. Existing main benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate theoretical guidance and GAN-loss choice, quantify mode coverage, examine failure at NFE=1–2, compare S4S parameterizations under shared settings, and inspect learned timestep schedules. Existing convergence, transfer, and adversarial-weight analyses remain, moving from B.1–B.3 to B.3–B.5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The random-seed information for displayed samples is retained. New diversity metrics are point estimates, not additions to uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 5–6 and 8–11 and Figure 7. Examples include FFHQ NFE=4 FID of 10.70 with guidance versus 15.23 without, and ImageNet GS/GAS recall of 0.63/0.76. New low-NFE results expose poor quality. Table 10's S4S results use a separate protocol rather than replacing Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction and Algorithm 1 are retained without substantive new derivations, assumptions, or proofs. The multistep coefficient's time-argument notation is clarified consistently with dependence already expressed elsewhere in v1. Learned-timestep properties are examined empirically, not proved.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions. Section 5 adds a claim that GS/GAS better preserve the original model's generative capabilities than distillation-based methods, while explicitly qualifying performance at NFE=1–2.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explicit low-NFE failure boundary attributed to limited trainable parameters, interprets relativistic loss as helpful but optional, and discusses coverage preservation relative to CD. Appendix E explains the observed validity of decoupled timesteps, including a slightly above-one value. Existing scalability and transfer limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new experiments document CD's official checkpoint and implementation, ternary search, T4096-based evaluation, and shared-codebase and initialization details for ablations. The existing algorithm, main hyperparameter lists, hardware reports, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Naeem et al. (2020) for fidelity/diversity metrics and develops positioning relative to the already-cited consistency-distillation approach. The related-work appendix and central positioning among solver-training methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized language corrections, a design-choice summary, explanatory sentences, additional appendix subsections and cross-references, and updated affiliations, publication header, and acknowledgments. The main narrative structure and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: Six new result tables substantially expand the experimental displays, covering component effects, diversity, comparisons, and low-NFE behavior. New Figure 7 provides a multipanel timestep visualization, and Figure 2 is revised. Existing sample galleries are retained and renumbered from Figures 7–24 to Figures 8–25.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its no-mode-collapse claim mainly through samples and FID; v2 adds direct diversity measurements and controlled ablations that better isolate central design choices. It also documents the important NFE=1–2 failure boundary. These additions substantially strengthen evidential support and clarify applicability. The CD comparison has a tradeoff: GS/GAS achieve higher coverage but worse FID in Table 9, supporting a narrower advantage rather than overall superiority.
